meta.title: Separation versus breakup discrimination
meta.authored_by: Claude Opus (illustrative draft, pending Ash authoring)
meta.change_reason: ILLUSTRATIVE content authored to exercise the drill loop, the scoring engine and the interface end to end. Derived only from public open-source material on space domain awareness practice, per the flight plan's public-sources rule. It is NOT a JCO procedure and has not been authored or validated by a subject-matter expert. Ash owns authoring and redaction sign-off; every step, threshold and answer key here is TBC, re-verify.

purpose: Decide whether newly associated objects are a deliberate separation or a fragmentation, because the two demand different responses and look similar in the first hours.
entry_conditions: One or more new objects correlate to the vicinity of a known parent object.
An uncorrelated track appears close to a known object in both position and time.
A brightness change on a known object coincides with new nearby detections.

steps.action: Count the associated objects and characterise how the count is growing over time.
steps.note: A handful of pieces that stops growing points one way. A count that keeps climbing as sensors revisit points the other.

steps.action: Examine the spread of the pieces in period and altitude.
steps.note: A fragmentation spreads energy across a wide, roughly symmetric band. A separation produces a small number of pieces with a narrow, often single-signed offset.

steps.action: Assess whether any piece is manoeuvring.
steps.warning: A piece under control is decisive evidence against fragmentation. A piece that is not manoeuvring proves nothing either way.

steps.action: Check whether the parent object survives and remains under control.
Classify as deliberate separation, fragmentation, or indeterminate, and state confidence.
Check the parent and any protected neighbours against the criteria held outside this application.
Report at the threshold the criteria set, and flag the debris hazard separately from the intent assessment.
steps.note: Hazard and intent are different questions on different clocks. Conflating them delays one of them.

threshold_criteria.name: piece-count-stable
threshold_criteria.condition: The associated object count stops growing after sensor revisit rather than continuing to climb.

threshold_criteria.name: narrow-energy-spread
threshold_criteria.condition: The pieces occupy a narrow period and altitude band consistent with a low-energy separation.

threshold_criteria.name: piece-under-control
threshold_criteria.condition: At least one associated object shows evidence of controlled manoeuvre.

threshold_criteria.name: parent-intact
threshold_criteria.condition: The parent object continues to be tracked and continues to behave as controlled.

reporting_requirements: Parent designator and the count of associated objects, with the time the count was taken.
The observed spread in period and altitude.
Whether any piece is under control, and the evidence.
Classification and confidence, with the debris hazard reported separately from intent.

transition_rules.when: A separated piece begins a controlled close approach to another object.
The parent is assessed as having manoeuvred rather than separated.

closure_criteria: All associated objects are catalogued and under routine custody.
The event is confirmed as a fragmentation and handed to debris assessment.
